content:
For programs that could reasonably be verified using either Verus or Aeneas+Lean, what are the main practical or technical reasons to choose Aeneas+Lean? Is it primarily because of capabilities that Lean provides beyond Verus, or are there other important differences in the verification workflow, expressiveness, automation, maintainability, or kinds of properties that can be proved?

Conversely, what kinds of Rust verification problems are currently better suited to Verus than to Aeneas+Lean?

Not saying that you won't find people here who can answer your question, you probably will, but it might also be interesting to post this question in the Aeneas Zulip: https://aeneas-verif.zulipchat.com Just mentioning it in case you were not aware of its existence

This have been discussed on zulip before, a quick search should find it.
I also have a partially verified version of Hax in lean, Aeneas' sister:
https://github.com/spitters/hax-lean
